A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same RSR/RSR++ study with readable text, equations, figures and tables. Both contain 13 pages ending with references; neither includes an appendix.

before.justification: Section 6 and Figures 5–9 report original matrix-multiplication timing, memory and block-size experiments using C++ and NumPy implementations.

after.justification: Section 6 and Figures 5–9 retain the same original empirical timing, memory and block-size results.

M1.justification: The ternary-to-binary reduction, column blocking, row permutation, segmentation and RSR/RSR++ inference procedures remain unchanged in Sections 3–5 and Algorithms 1–3.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic binary and ternary vector–matrix multiplication. No dataset, task, domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The C++ experiments retain Standard, RSR and RSR++, while the NumPy experiments retain RSR versus np.dot(). Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 6 retains the same random input generation, matrix-size sweeps, optimal-k selection and runtime/memory evaluation procedures. No experimental setting or protocol is revised.

E4.justification: The block-size optimization analysis in Figure 7 and the RSR-versus-RSR++ analysis in Figure 6 are unchanged. No additional ablation or robustness analysis appears.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over 10 runs in Figure 5 and four runs in Figure 8. Run-count disclosures and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical results and plotted trends match throughout Figures 5–9. For example, Figure 5 retains the 29.55x RSR++ speedup over Standard, and Figure 9 retains the 5.99x memory reduction.

T1.justification: The definitions, lemmas, proofs and complexity guarantees in Sections 3–5 are unchanged. Removing the word 'Permute' from Equation 2 does not alter its mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same algorithms, logarithmic time/storage claims and headline gains. The new title's binary/ternary neural-network scope was already stated in v1.

C2.justification: The interpretations and Section 7 discussion remain unchanged, including preprocessing costs, RSR++ parallelization limitations and generalization to rectangular and q-bit matrices.

D1.justification: The C++/NumPy implementation descriptions, parameter-selection details and public RSR repository link are unchanged. No technical or reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning against hardware-level matrix-multiplication acceleration are unchanged. The revised title does not establish a different novelty claim or relationship to prior work.

P1.justification: The title shifts from 'Optimized Inference for 1.58-bit LLMs...' to 'An Efficient Matrix Multiplication Algorithm for Accelerating Inference in Binary and Ternary Neural Networks.' Running headers change, and the GPT-3 illustration changes 'up to' to 'at least up to.' Section order and nearly all prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Running headers use the new title and drop 'Preprint'; pages 2–3 have slight text reflow, and Equation 2 loses its 'Permute' label. Figures 1–9 and Table 1 retain their content and presentation.

improvement.justification: The revision makes limited title, wording and formatting adjustments while retaining the methods, mathematical support, empirical evidence, limitations and reproducibility information. These editorial changes do not establish a meaningful net improvement or deterioration in overall paper quality.
